svg.title: The stones in three lists
svg.desc: A drawn plate in three parts. First, the high priest's breastpiece from Exodus 28:17-20 as a gold frame holding twelve stones in four rows of three. Each stone shows its Hebrew name and transliteration, the Septuagint's Greek name, the ESV's English name, and a coloured swatch showing the stone the Greek name meant according to Pliny: 1, ʾodem, Greek σάρδιον, ESV sardius; 2, pitdah, Greek τοπάζιον, ESV topaz; 3, bareqet, Greek σμάραγδος, ESV carbuncle; 4, nofekh, Greek ἄνθραξ, ESV emerald; 5, sappir, Greek σάπφειρος, ESV sapphire; 6, yahalom, Greek ἴασπις, ESV diamond; 7, leshem, Greek λιγύριον, ESV jacinth; 8, shevo, Greek ἀχάτης, ESV agate; 9, ʾachlamah, Greek ἀμέθυστος, ESV amethyst; 10, tarshish, Greek χρυσόλιθος, ESV beryl; 11, shoham, Greek βηρύλλιον, ESV onyx; 12, yashpeh, Greek ὀνύχιον, ESV jasper. Stones 1 to 6 and 10 to 12 are marked as named in the Hebrew of Ezekiel 28:13; the third row is not. A note says the Greek of Ezekiel 28:13 names all twelve in the same order, with silver and gold after the sixth. Second, the twelve foundations of the city from Revelation 21:19-20 as stacked bands: 1st, Greek ἴασπις, ESV jasper, breastpiece number 6; 2nd, Greek σάπφειρος, ESV sapphire, breastpiece number 5; 3rd, Greek χαλκηδών, ESV agate, not on the breastpiece; 4th, Greek σμάραγδος, ESV emerald, breastpiece number 3; 5th, Greek σαρδόνυξ, ESV onyx, sard and onyx in one stone; 6th, Greek σάρδιον, ESV carnelian, breastpiece number 1; 7th, Greek χρυσόλιθος, ESV chrysolite, breastpiece number 10; 8th, Greek βήρυλλος, ESV beryl, breastpiece number 11; 9th, Greek τοπάζιον, ESV topaz, breastpiece number 2; 10th, Greek χρυσόπρασος, ESV chrysoprase, not on the breastpiece; 11th, Greek ὑάκινθος, ESV jacinth, not on the breastpiece; 12th, Greek ἀμέθυστος, ESV amethyst, breastpiece number 9. Eight foundations share their Greek name with a breastpiece stone. Ligyrion, chalcedon and hyacinth have dashed swatches because their identification is uncertain. Third, a key and Revelation 21:23: the glory of God gives the city light, and its lamp is the Lamb.
svg.text: The breastpiece: twelve stones in four rows, each engraved with a tribe's name
(Exodus 28:17-21). Hebrew, then the Septuagint's Greek, then the ESV.
Ezekiel 28:13 (Hebrew) names the nine marked “Ezek 28”: every row but the third.
The Greek of Ezekiel 28:13 names all twelve in this order, with silver and gold after the sixth.
sard and onyx in one stone
Colour of the stone the Greek name meant (Pliny, Natural History 37)
Which stone the ancient name meant is uncertain
A foundation whose stone is not on the breastpiece
The ESV’s English often follows a different identification from the swatch.
“The city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, for the glory of God
gives it light, and its lamp is the Lamb.”
After the manner of Clarence Larkin · the-way.lewy.au
